correctness.rationale: Equation (3) is obtained by multiplying absolutely convergent Poisson Fourier series by the two cosines. The exhaustive index regimes in (4) show that the two mixed-quadrant inequalities are necessary, while their sum forces strictly positive zero-index Fourier coefficients using equation (6). This supplies exact sufficiency through compact abelian Bochner. All positive characters give universality; at a nonvertex facet one positive mixed quadrant forces every finite coefficient vector to vanish by two Vandermonde inversions. At the vertex the support is exactly the two coordinate axes, so Gram nullvectors are precisely bipartite incidence nullvectors, of dimension E-V+c. The rational checker independently verified 1,452 Fourier class identities, three exact 6-point Gram ranks/eigenvalue signs and apex axial identities. Finite computations are not offered as proof of universal quantifiers.

value.rationale: The two mixed first harmonics are the lowest-order nonseparable signed perturbation of a standard stationary product Poisson covariance. The theorem completely determines their admissible region, its two different spectral edge phases, and the sole transition from finite-site strictness to graph-cycle singularity. Unlike a numerical finite table, the formula gives all real parameters and all finite sample geometries. The distinction of strict finite-site positive definiteness, C-universality, and exact cycle-rank degeneracy is relevant for covariance design and interpolation geometry, without claiming a downstream theorem.
